title: Handling Feature Heterogeneity with Learnable Graph Patches

problem.claim: Graph foundation models need to transfer across graph datasets with heterogeneous features.

gap.claim: Existing models cannot address feature heterogeneity in graph data without textual information, limiting transferability across datasets.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces learnable graph patches as semantic units of graph data.
PatchNet decomposes graphs into learnable patches and combines a patch encoder with a patch aggregator to mine transferable information across domains.
The paper analyzes PatchNet's connection to existing graph models and the transferability of its generated node embeddings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method reportedly enables pre-training with multi-domain graphs and improves performance across downstream datasets and tasks.
The authors report consistent downstream performance improvement as pre-training data volume increases.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph foundation models are being pursued as universal pre-trained graph models.
Feature heterogeneity without textual information limits transferability across graph datasets.
The paper represents graphs as learnable patches, decomposes node features and patch structures, and processes them with PatchNet's encoder and aggregator.
The domain-agnostic model is intended for downstream data across different domains, with analyses of model connections and embedding transferability.
The authors report multi-domain pre-training, improved downstream performance, and further gains with more pre-training data.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, tasks, baselines, metrics, or numerical performance gains.
The abstract does not describe the pre-training data scale or the conditions under which feature heterogeneity is evaluated.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or independent verification.
